name: Community
tagline: Who lives here, how that is changing, what is being built, and what the township's own services record.
primer: Almost everything in this domain comes from Statistics Canada, and almost every problem in this domain comes from geography. The census subdivision called North Glengarry matches the municipal boundary, which makes population, dwelling, and household counts directly usable. Below that level the geographies stop matching anything a council recognises: dissemination areas cross settlement boundaries, and the census agglomerations used for labour force reporting cover territory well beyond the township. A figure quoted at the wrong geography is not slightly wrong, it is about a different place.

The second constraint is timing. The census is quinquennial. Between cycles there is no authoritative population count, only estimates, and municipal population estimates for small rural municipalities carry meaningful error. Trend in this domain is measured in five-year steps, and any annual series purporting to describe township population is an estimate that must be labelled as one.

Age structure is the demographic fact that drives the most municipal consequence, because it moves slowly and predictably and shows up in service demand a decade later. The dependency ratio — population under fifteen and over sixty-four against the working-age population — is the compact form of it. In rural Eastern Ontario the older end of that ratio is generally the one that moves.

Building permits are the township's own record and are available annually, which makes them the most timely growth signal available. They come with two cautions. Declared construction value is the applicant's figure for fee purposes and is neither a market value nor an assessed value. And a permit is a plan, not a building: permits issued and units completed diverge, particularly when financing conditions change between application and construction.

Agriculture is the dominant land use in North Glengarry and the Census of Agriculture is the only consistent series describing it. Farm counts falling while average farm area rises is consolidation rather than decline, and the two figures have to be read together or the story is inverted. Operator age is the leading indicator in this sector, because it forecasts land transfer.

The service statistics at the end of this domain — library, recreation, facility usage — are the township's own numbers and are the least standardised data in the dashboard. They are worth carrying anyway: they are the only place where residents' actual use of what the township provides is recorded at all, and the Ontario Public Library Statistics submission gives at least the library a comparable multi-year basis.

tierSplit.note: Township issues permits and employs the Chief Building Official.
Delivered by the SDG County Library, established 1971 from the merger of seven rural libraries. Not a township library board — a common and consequential misattribution.
SDG is the consolidated municipal service manager. Waitlists are reported county-wide.
County is the service system manager.
Both tiers run programmes. Confirm the current division and any joint funding agreement.

gaps: Business openings and closures have no authoritative municipal source. Business licence data covers only licensed categories, which in a rural township is a small share of businesses. Any count here is partial by construction and must be labelled so.

Employment and labour force figures are not reliably available at the township level. The smallest geography with acceptable error is larger than the township and must be named wherever such a figure appears.
Tourism has no municipal measurement instrument. Accommodation counts and event attendance may be obtainable but are not a series.
Recreation registration and facility usage are reported inconsistently between years and may require manual entry from budget presentations.

Library statistics are reported for the county system as a whole. Branch-level circulation, membership, and programming for the North Glengarry branches are not published and must be requested from the county library.

indicators.geography: North Glengarry, Township (census subdivision) — boundary matches the municipality
indicators.tierNote: Counted by Statistics Canada. The township does not produce its own count.
indicators.definition: Total population on census day at the census subdivision, whose boundary matches the municipal boundary. Census counts are subject to undercoverage, which Statistics Canada estimates separately; the count shown is the published count, not the adjusted estimate.

source.locator: Focus on Geography, population change 2006 to 2011

series.note: Back-calculated from the stated -3.6 percent change between 2006 and 2011, not read from a 2006 profile. Replace with the figure read directly.

Two figures circulate for 2021: 10,144 and 10,119. This dashboard records 10,144 and does not reconcile the difference silently. Confirm against the Statistics Canada profile table directly and record which is the published count.

indicators.methodology: Census subdivision 3501050, geographic identifier 2021A00053501050. The township covers 643.4 square kilometres, giving a population density of about 15.8 people per square kilometre in 2021 — the figure that explains why service delivery here costs what it does per resident.

indicators.name: Median age
indicators.definition: Age at which half the population is older and half younger. A single figure summarising age structure; the full distribution is in the detail table and is more useful for service planning.

indicators.name: Age dependency ratio
indicators.definition: Population aged under 15 plus population aged 65 and over, per 100 people aged 15 to 64. A demographic measure of the ratio between ages typically outside the labour force and ages typically within it. It describes age structure only and says nothing about employment, income, or need.

indicators.name: Occupied private dwellings
indicators.definition: Count of private dwellings occupied by usual residents on census day. Used as the denominator for the per-household figures in the financial domain.

series.note: 4,422 of 4,714 total private dwellings were occupied by usual residents. The 292 unoccupied dwellings are seasonal, vacant, or occupied only by foreign or temporary residents.

indicators.name: Residential building permits issued
indicators.definition: Count of residential building permits issued during the calendar year, all residential types including additions and renovations where a permit is required. A permit issued is not a dwelling completed.

indicators.name: Declared construction value, all permits
indicators.definition: Total construction value declared on permit applications during the year. Declared for fee-setting purposes by the applicant. It is not a market value, not an assessed value, and not audited.

indicators.name: Census farms
indicators.geography: North Glengarry, Township (census consolidated subdivision) — verify this matches the municipal boundary before quoting
indicators.definition: Number of agricultural operations reporting in the Census of Agriculture. Read alongside total farm area: a falling count with rising average area is consolidation, which has different implications than a falling count with falling area.

indicators.name: Library circulation, county system
indicators.geography: Stormont, Dundas and Glengarry County Library service area — not the township alone
indicators.definition: Total items circulated during the year across the county library system, physical and electronic combined. The county system was established in 1971 from the merger of seven existing rural libraries. Because the reporting unit is the county system, this figure must not be attributed to North Glengarry. The 2020 and 2021 values reflect a period of restricted in-person service.

tables.title: Age structure
tables.description: Shares by age group across three census cycles. Movement between cycles is what forecasts service demand: the group aged 55 to 64 in one cycle is the group aged 65 to 74 in the next.

tables.title: Households by tenure and dwelling type
tables.description: Tenure and dwelling type together describe the housing stock the township actually has, which constrains what kinds of household can move here.
tables.note: Tenure rows and dwelling-type rows are two separate breakdowns of the same household total and should not be added together.

tables.title: Agriculture profile
tables.description: Farm counts, area, and operator age across three agricultural census cycles. Operator age is the leading indicator for land transfer and the succession question that follows it.
tables.geography: North Glengarry — census consolidated subdivision. Confirm boundary alignment with the municipality.
tables.note: Operator counts and farm counts are different denominators — a farm may report more than one operator.
